title: Making a Design Culture
subtitle: A Critical Dialogue on Agency, Experimentation, and Material Capacity
abstract: A design culture gains depth when people can direct ideas, investigate possibilities, translate knowledge into material form, engage the public, and build expertise over time.

This paper presents a curated critical dialogue between Brandie Janow, Harry Dobbs, and Paulo Pimentel, convened in May 2026 in preparation for Knowledge of Design’s first international session. The discussion examines agency, provenance, experimentation, making, public value, and the pace of cultural and industrial development.
A thematic review identified five connected conditions: agency, original practice, experimentation, material capacity, and public life over time.

Grounded in Saudi Arabia’s current period of cultural and industrial development, the dialogue considers questions that extend beyond one geography: how emerging fields establish their own standards, how international expertise can deepen local authorship, and how technical confidence develops through material experience over time.
research_question: What enables a design culture to develop through original practice, material capacity, public relevance, and ongoing growth?

framework.definition: The ability to frame questions, exercise judgment, and influence direction.
Grows through inquiry, observation, and the confidence to create beyond familiar references.
Gives practitioners room to test possibilities, learn through process, and refine their judgment.
Connects ideas with the tools, skills, and production knowledge required to bring them into use.
Gives design the opportunity to be encountered, evaluated, supported, and revised across generations.
